{author:"A Geomancer",filtered_title:"Measure of Ston",pages:['{"text":"Day 3 - The First Bow\\n\\nToday I learned the first rule of the Earthrend way: before touching stone, bow to it. Not because rock is a god, but because the hand that refuses respect will always reach for violence. The monastery steps are chipped and"}','{"text":"wind-worn, and still they stand straighter than most who come here."}','{"text":"Day 7 - Quite Hands\\n\\nmy teacher corrected me without raising his void. In geomancy, the earth does not respond to shouting hearts. It answers to a will that is settled. I have begun to practive holding my breath util my thoughts stop jostling each other."}','{"text":"Day 20 - Trials are Not Punishments\\n\\nThe courtyard is a classroom disguised as a challenge. Ledges are set at awkward angles. Gaps are spaced to humble the legs. The trial isn\'t here to break disciples, only to show them to themselves."}','{"text":"A proud climber falls early. A rushed climber falls often. The one who climbs with manners - patient, careful, paying attention - starts to feel even harsh stone guiding them."}','{"text":"Day 31 - What We Believe\\n\\nWe do not worship the earth as a jealous power that demands to be fed. We honor it as a teacher: enduring, honest, unhurried. The mountains do not flatter. If the stone refuses you, it is not spite - it is instruction."}','{"text":"Day 32 - Where Water Turns Strange\\n\\nSome speak of the Aquamancers, and how their art comes from places where light does not reach. Their old belief, their \\"god\\", promised power without patience, and many of them paid with their minds until they resembled the things"}','{"text":"that first whispered to them. Yet there is a grim courage in their path: to master aqua, they learn to hold corruption by the throat and keep breathing anyway - gripping the storm inside their skull until it obeys."}','{"text":"Day 45 - The Meaning of Defeat\\n\\nIf you ever cross blades with one of us and you prevail, understand it for what it is. In our tradition, a duel is not an ending - it is a turning. Rank is not owned forever. It is held, and can be taken by steadier hand."}','{"text":"Day 61 - For Those Who Finds This\\n\\nDo not demand for shortcuts to them. If you truly seek Geomancy, let the first spell you learn be a simple one:\\n\\n        Restraint"}'],resolved:1b,title:"Measure of Stone"}

functions.tag: {title:"Quiet House Journal",author:"Mara Vell",pages:['{"text":"I keep the shutters closed now. The raiders came like a storm from the west, not villagers, not pillagers I know. They carried no banners, only a low hum like flies."}','{"text":"We left in the night. I barred the door, buried the key beneath the step, and walked east with only bread and my mother\'s quilt. If you are reading this, do not wait for them to pass."}']}

{title:"Notes on Turning Power",author:"Gareth Holt",pages:['{"text":"I lashed a wheel to the stream and found a strange comfort in its steady pull. The turn never tires. With gears and a shaft, the motion climbs the stairs to the loft."}','{"text":"If I can store this rotation, I can drive a press and grind grain without a mule. Call it rotational force. It feels like a secret the river has been keeping."}']}

{title:"On Bitter Brews",author:"Selene",pages:['{"text":"Always mark the red bottles. A draught of Healing can mend a cut, but it will not mend a burnt tongue."}','{"text":"Swiftness needs sugar. Water Breathing needs pufferfish. The mix curdles if heated too long. I tried it on a stray cat; it hissed and dove into the basin without fear."}']}

{title:"Poison Notes",author:"Krell",pages:['{"text":"Fermented spider eye turns a clear potion sour. The first sip is sweet, the second is trouble."}','{"text":"Weakness comes from a steady hand and a small dose. I tested on mice and a coop hen. The hen glared, but lived."}']}

{title:"Quiet Sorceries",author:"R. Thatch",pages:['{"text":"Some pages whisper about binding shadows and bending will. I keep them locked and read them once, with a candle and a steady door."}','{"text":"Invisibility takes the night and a golden carrot. Night Vision takes the glow of a carrot and a spider\'s eye. If the recipe asks for a Wither Rose, close the book."}']}

{title:"Bazaar Ledger: Day 18",author:"Rafiq",pages:['{"text":"Bought 12 pieces of leather, sold 9. Paid two emeralds in shade money to keep the awning up."}','{"text":"Water price doubled at noon. A caravan from the south brought dates and cracked pottery. The pottery still sold."}']}

{title:"Salt and Silk",author:"Minaq",pages:['{"text":"Traded six sacks of salt for one chest of silk. The buyer swore it was moon-white. It was off-white, but soft."}','{"text":"Reminder: copper ingots carry better than coins in the dunes. Coins clink. Raiders listen."}']}

{title:"Caravan Log: West Dunes",author:"Jalen",pages:['{"text":"Three wagons lost a wheel on day two. Replaced with acacia and a prayer."}','{"text":"Scorpions at camp, but the camels held steady. Found a shrine of bleached stone and left a coin."}']}

{title:"Stall Rules, Written Small",author:"Bazaar Clerk",pages:['{"text":"No sales during the bell. No shouting over the spice guild. Keep blades sheathed after dusk."}','{"text":"If a trade is disputed, walk to the blue tent. Do not argue in the sand."}']}

{title:"The Labyrinth",author:"Old Nura",pages:['{"text":"There is a maze out in the deep desert. Stone walls, no shade, a treasure at its heart if the stories are true."}','{"text":"The sand keeps its own secrets. If you go, mark your way. If you return, bring water for the next fool."}']}

{title:"Missing Crates",author:"Safa",pages:['{"text":"Two crates of glass beads vanished between the north gate and stall 14. Guards blame wind. Wind does not lock latches."}','{"text":"If found, return for double pay. If not found, I will find you."}']}

{title:"Map Without a Map",author:"Tamar",pages:['{"text":"Walk by the sun when it kisses the far dune. The stone finger points west. The dry well is your last shade."}','{"text":"If the wind buries the markers, trust the stars and the taste of the air. It always turns iron before a storm."}']}

{title:"Bearclaw Night Notes",author:"Ivy",pages:['{"text":"The bar below never really sleeps. The floor hums with singing, the rafters with stomping."}','{"text":"Upstairs, the quilts are soft and the windows hold the cold out. Cozy enough to make you forget the world is wide."}']}

{title:"Ale and Snow",author:"Doran Pike",pages:['{"text":"Met a cartographer who swore the mountain pass was haunted. He drank two mugs and drew a map that looked like a bear."}','{"text":"The innkeep laughed. The fire roared. The map was wrong, but the story was worth the coin."}']}

{title:"Quiet Room, Loud Bar",author:"Mara",pages:['{"text":"I only meant to rest a night. Stayed three. The bar noise is a kind of blanket if you let it be."}','{"text":"A hunter told me of a frozen cave with blue light. I told him I prefer warm bread and a door that latches."}']}

{title:"Bee Notes",author:"Elin",pages:['{"text":"Put a campfire under the hive and the bees stay calm. Smoke makes them slow, not angry."}','{"text":"Flowers nearby keep the hive busy. A quiet yard is a full jar."}']}

{title:"Honey Primer",author:"Elin",pages:['{"text":"Bottles for honey, shears for honeycomb. Never take both on the same day unless you want to be chased."}','{"text":"Honey blocks slow a fall. I keep a stack by the ladder in case a guest forgets their feet."}']}

{title:"Honeyed Apples",author:"Elin",pages:['{"text":"Slice apples, coat in honey, and stir in a basin until they shine. The Create folks call them honeyed apples."}','{"text":"Best eaten warm by the window while the bees drift home."}']}

{title:"Flax Field Notes",author:"Vera",pages:['{"text":"Flax likes light and room to breathe. Water the rows, then let them dry between storms."}','{"text":"Harvest the stalks and twist the fibers. Supplementaries rope is best when the strands are still soft."}']}

{title:"Greenhouse Uses",author:"Vera",pages:['{"text":"Cornflower for blue dye, rose for red. Mushrooms for stew, moss for quiet floors."}','{"text":"Never waste seeds. A compost pile is just a future harvest."}']}

{title:"Plant List for Trade",author:"Vera",pages:['{"text":"Wheat for bread, carrots for stews, sugar cane for paper. Lilacs sell well if bundled."}','{"text":"The town wants more rope, so plant extra flax by the fence."}']}

{title:"Leaving the Brickhouse",author:"Nell",pages:['{"text":"I grew tired of the quiet here. The oven is warm but the rooms are too still."}','{"text":"I am leaving to find a better life and someone to share these cookies with. If you find this, take one."}']}

{title:"Brick and Bread",author:"Nell",pages:['{"text":"Repairs on the north wall hold. I patched the roof with spare tiles and a prayer."}','{"text":"Baked three loaves, left one on the sill for the fox. It did not leave a thank-you note."}']}

{title:"Tax Day Notes",author:"Sera",pages:['{"text":"Another levy today. Three emeralds per household, and the steward still smiles."}','{"text":"We keep quiet in the hall, but the muttering grows. A crown should not weigh this much on a common back."}']}

{title:"Castle Kitchen List",author:"Mills",pages:['{"text":"Bread, rabbit stew, four honeyed apples for the captain. No more beets without salt."}','{"text":"If the banquet is late again, serve the guards first. They keep the peace with empty bellies."}']}

{title:"Quiet Council Notes",author:"C. Alder",pages:['{"text":"The taxes climb again. The king wants emeralds for every wall and banner."}','{"text":"If he will not listen, we will make him listen. Meet by the old armory after dusk."}']}

{title:"Petition Draft",author:"Hale",pages:['{"text":"We ask for relief and a fair tally. We have paid too many emeralds and too many nights."}','{"text":"If the crown refuses, then the crown will change. The ink dries at midnight."}']}

{title:"Guard Roster",author:"Captain Ryn",pages:['{"text":"North wall: two on, two off. South gate: rotate at bell."}','{"text":"No sleeping on watch. If you see torch signals, report to the steward."}']}

{title:"Library Inventory",author:"Archivist Lume",pages:['{"text":"Missing: On Old Kings and Ledger of War. Both borrowed and never returned."}','{"text":"Dust the east shelf weekly. Rats have taken a liking to the binding glue."}']}

{title:"Sherd Notes",author:"Kelm",pages:['{"text":"Brushed up three sherds today. One shows a spiral, another a fish, the third a small house."}','{"text":"The clay is old but the stories are clear. Handle with care and a steady hand."}']}

{title:"Eggshell Fragments",author:"Rhea",pages:['{"text":"Found curved fragments the size of my palm. They are too thick for turtle, too smooth for dragon myth."}','{"text":"Maybe huge old eggs, maybe just wishful thinking. Either way, the soil remembers something big."}']}

{title:"Desert Sherd Log",author:"Kelm",pages:['{"text":"The sand keeps swallowing our markers. Still, the brush finds shapes: a camel, a sun, a tall jar."}','{"text":"We wrap each piece and stack them by the tent. The wind wants them back."}']}

{title:"Field Notes: Giant Eggs",author:"Rhea",pages:['{"text":"Bone shards and a ring of shell, half-buried. Old as the dunes."}','{"text":"We argue whether it was a nest or a shrine. Either way, the eggs were enormous."}']}

{title:"Rooms Upstairs",author:"Edwin Pike",pages:['{"text":"Three guests again tonight. The miller snores, the shepherd talks in his sleep, and someone keeps taking the candle from the hall sconce.\\n\\nIf it happens once more, I am charging extra."}','{"text":"Note to self: patch the loose floorboard near the window before someone twists an ankle. Also buy more soap, and keep the good goblet downstairs where it belongs."}','{"text":"The lady in blue asked whether this place was haunted. I told her only by unpaid tabs. She laughed. Good sign."}']}

{title:"A Guest's Diary",author:"Mira Holt",pages:['{"text":"The Tudor Pub is warmer than it looks from the road. The bed creaks, but the stew is honest and the innkeep remembers names, which is more than most do."}','{"text":"I heard wagon bells past midnight and boots in the yard before dawn. Trade never really stops here. Even the walls seem tired."}']}

{title:"On Inns",author:"R. Thorne",pages:['{"text":"Stayed at the Bearclaw Inn two nights prior. Cleaner floors, worse company."}','{"text":"The Tudor Pub lacks polish but has warmth. The fire is real, the bread is fresh."}','{"text":"Bearclaw has coin. Tudor has soul."}']}

{title:"Kitchen Notes",author:"Marta",pages:['{"text":"Stew for six:\\n3 potatoes\\n2 carrots\\n1 beet if it is turning soft anyway\\nSalt if we have it\\n\\nDo not let Tovin near the pot before noon."}','{"text":"Bread rises better by the hearth than by the back wall. Remind Edwin that flour sacks are not to be stacked under the leaky beam."}','{"text":"The whisk went missing again. If the stable boy is using it as a toy sword, I am telling his mother."}']}

{title:"Strange Talk",author:"Marta",pages:['{"text":"Trader came through talking nonsense again."}','{"text":"Says there is a tree taller than a tower, bark shaped like a face."}','{"text":"Says it watches. I say he drinks too much."}']}

{title:"Delivery Record",author:"Tovin",pages:['{"text":"Received this week:\\n2 coils rope\\n1 bar soap crate\\n3 paper bundles\\n1 copper patch plate\\n\\nMissing: lamp oil again."}','{"text":"Store dry goods off the floor. Rats got into the back sack last rain. Edwin says trap them. Marta says name them and charge rent."}','{"text":"If anyone asks where the spare sconce went, I lent it to the room upstairs after the hall one cracked. I did mean to write that down sooner."}']}

{title:"Ledger of Tabs",author:"Edwin Pike",pages:['{"text":"Tabs owed:\\nHarlan - 4 mugs\\nMira - paid\\nOld Fen - 2 ciders\\nMason twins - never again."}','{"text":"Business steady. Repaired copper kettle again."}','{"text":"Money comes and goes faster than ale."}']}

{title:"Butcher's Ledger",author:"Dolan Marr",pages:['{"text":"Meat sells quickest when the weather is poor and folk would rather buy supper than hunt it."}','{"text":"Waste nothing. Hide, bone, and fat all have buyers if you know who asks quietly."}','{"text":"A clean block and a sharp blade earn trust faster than a smiling face."}']}

{title:"Kinetic Basics",author:"Orin Vale",pages:['{"text":"Start simple: shafts, cogwheels, casing, and a hand crank if all else fails."}','{"text":"Do not chase fancy metal before learning the humble machine. A millstone used well earns more than a complicated contraption built poorly."}','{"text":"If it spins and screams, slow it down. If it spins and works, pretend you meant it that way."}']}

{title:"On Crystals",author:"Sel the Polisher",pages:['{"text":"Common folk buy color before quality. Red sells first, blue sells steady, and violet sits until someone falls in love with it."}','{"text":"Clusters fetch more attention than loose pieces. Leave some stone on them and call it natural beauty."}','{"text":"Do not display everything in direct sun. Some stones lose wonder when seen too plainly."}']}

{title:"Field Notes",author:"Maren Hill",pages:['{"text":"A tidy field is half the harvest. Keep seed dry, rows straight, and tools where they belong."}','{"text":"Do not plant everything at once unless you enjoy panic all in the same week."}','{"text":"Hay keeps, grain trades, and seed is hope made small enough to fit in a pocket."}']}

{title:"River Advice",author:"Cob Finn",pages:['{"text":"A fisherman sells patience, not just fish. Cast where the water changes color and watch the drift."}','{"text":"Shells and odd catches fetch more coin from collectors than they do from hungry folk."}','{"text":"Never trust still water that looks too clean. The deep keeps its own mood."}']}

{title:"Showroom Notes",author:"Pella Reed",pages:['{"text":"A chair is bought with the eye before it is trusted by the back."}','{"text":"Stools sell fastest to workshops and kitchens. Seats sell to folk who want a room to feel finished."}','{"text":"Never stack the polished pieces near the entry. Dust travels faster than customers."}']}

{title:"Garden Keeper's Guide",author:"Edda Bloom",pages:['{"text":"A proper garden is more patience than grandeur. Pot the flowers, line the path, and keep the moss where it pleases the eye."}','{"text":"Bone meal is useful, but not a substitute for care. Too much fuss and a plant grows ugly in spirit, even if green in leaf."}','{"text":"Vines and lily pads sell well to folk who want their homes to feel older than they are."}']}

{title:"Lunch Notes",author:"Nell",pages:['{"text":"Whoever keeps leaving muddy boots by the kitchen door is buying the next loaf."}','{"text":"Tea tin on the upper shelf. Do not sell the staff bread unless we are truly desperate."}']}

{title:"Miner's Notes",author:"Garrick Venn",pages:['{"text":"A good miner learns stone before ore. Coal and copper show easy enough, but patience finds the better veins."}','{"text":"If you are digging with purpose, remember this: iron favors the deeper dark, and diamonds deeper still. Mark your tunnels and mind your way back."}','{"text":"Zinc buyers pay fair coin these days. If you find a pale raw ore in the stone, do not toss it aside."}']}

{title:"Inventory Oddments",author:"Wimble Cross",pages:['{"text":"A general store survives on two truths: someone always needs string, and someone always forgets to bring a torch."}','{"text":"Abacus sold to a man who could not count, clipboard sold to a woman who already could. Business is funny that way."}','{"text":"Keep the cardboard dry or it turns to sad paper and arguments."}']}

{title:"Stockroom Log",author:"Wimble Cross",pages:['{"text":"Back room holds what the front forgets: spare paper, cord, boxes, and things too odd to display nicely."}','{"text":"If a crate is marked FRAGILE, that means do not put tools on it. This note should not need repeating."}','{"text":"Move damp stock first. Dry goods last. And if anyone asks, yes, we definitely know where everything is."}']}

                {\"text\":\"Seize one ghast tear, a spider's eye,
\"},

            }

lore.fallback: with a final wish to regrow
the lost nature of the Nether
Has a chance to drop gold
You can hide, but you can't
For in life all things return
to death, and in death all things
Drink the brew, and bide the danger,
Or wonder till it drives you mad;
What would have happened if you had?
Emits a brilliant light when dropped
Packs a fiery, yet powerful punch
Drains the life of its wielder
The longer you hold back the bow,
the more powerful the lightning you create
Drains the life of its slain victims
the longer you pull the bow.
Destroys ghast fireballs that it can see.
Drink the brew, and bide the danger,
Or wonder till it drives you mad;
What would have happened if you had?

{
          pages:[
              "[
                \"\",
                {\"text\":\"§lThe \"},
                {\"text\":\"§kREDACTED\"},
                {\"text\":\"§l:
\"},
                {\"text\":\"§lA Complete History

\"},
                {\"text\":\"We are an ancient
\"},
                {\"text\":\"race of \"},
                {\"text\":\"§kREDACTED
\"},
                {\"text\":\"travellers who hunted
\"},
                {\"text\":\"and gathered for
\"},
                {\"text\":\"food. Eventually, we
\"},
                {\"text\":\"settled down and
\"},
                {\"text\":\"began farming crops
\"},
                {\"text\":\"such as wheat,
\"},
                {\"text\":\"carrots, and
\"},
                {\"text\":\"potatoes\"},
                {\"text\":\".\"}
              ]",
              "[
                {\"text\":\"This gave us
\"},
                {\"text\":\"newfound time to build.
\"},
                {\"text\":\"Our passion is
\"},
                {\"text\":\"building, it is what
\"},
                {\"text\":\"makes us who we are.
\"},
                {\"text\":\"We built cities that
\"},
                {\"text\":\"stretched for
\"},
                {\"text\":\"hundreds of blocks.
\"},
                {\"text\":\"We were prospering.

\"},
                {\"text\":\"All that changed when
\"},
                {\"text\":\"the \"},
                {\"text\":\"§kREDACTED\"},
                {\"text\":\" came.\"}
              ]",
              "[
                {\"text\":\"The \"},
                {\"text\":\"§kREDACTED\"},
                {\"text\":\" forced
\"},
                {\"text\":\"us to flee. They
\"},
                {\"text\":\"burned our cities and
\"},
                {\"text\":\"fields. They destroyed
\"},
                {\"text\":\"our home. That is why
\"},
                {\"text\":\"we settled in this
\"},
                {\"text\":\"mighty Stronghold. It
\"},
                {\"text\":\"is a fortress
\"},
                {\"text\":\"underground that we
\"},
                {\"text\":\"hope they will never
\"},
                {\"text\":\"reach. Since then we
\"},
                {\"text\":\"have made a life for
\"},
                {\"text\":\"ourselves
\"},
                {\"text\":\"underground.\"}
              ]",
              "[
                {\"text\":\"We developed an
\"},
                {\"text\":\"entire society with no
\"},
                {\"text\":\"need of the sun or
\"},
                {\"text\":\"the light of day. We do
\"},
                {\"text\":\"everything from
\"},
                {\"text\":\"farming to \"},
                {\"text\":\"§kdreaming
\"},
                {\"text\":\"in this mighty
\"},
                {\"text\":\"underground
\"},
                {\"text\":\"fortress. Our
\"},
                {\"text\":\"researchers have
\"},
                {\"text\":\"even developed new
\"},
                {\"text\":\"technologies such as
\"},
                {\"text\":\"rotational power and
\"},
                {\"text\":\"§kdimensional travel\"},
                {\"text\":\".\"}
              ]",
              "[
                {\"text\":\"Since the faithful day
\"},
                {\"text\":\"that \"},
                {\"text\":\"§kasteroid\"},
                {\"text\":\" struck,
\"},
                {\"text\":\"we have looked to
\"},
                {\"text\":\"the skies for the
\"},
                {\"text\":\"mighty One Above All.
\"},
                {\"text\":\"We believe that one
\"},
                {\"text\":\"day, we will reunite
\"},
                {\"text\":\"with the One Above All
\"},
                {\"text\":\"to stop the \"},
                {\"text\":\"§kREDACTED
\"},
                {\"text\":\"and create a better
\"},
                {\"text\":\"world for all of its
\"},
                {\"text\":\"inhabitants.\"}
              ]"
            ],
            title:History,
            author:CraisinLord,
            display:{Lore:["Found in the ancient Stronghold"]}
            }

{filtered_title: "Hope Unmade", pages: ["{\"text\":\"And eventually I did it.\\n\\nThe barrier shattered. And just for a second - I let myself believe I have won.\"}", "{\"text\":\"\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBut I was wrong...\"}", "{\"text\":\"I think I cannot continue this journal anym......\"}"], title: "Hope Unmade", author: "??????", resolved: 1}

{filtered_title: "Lost One", pages: ["{\"text\":\"She was taken. Lost to the End by something I couldn't name. No sign, no warning, no clue - just silence. Whatever it was, it left nothing behind but questions.\\n\\n\"}"], title: "Lost One", author: "???", resolved: 1}

{author:"GameTechBC",filtered_title:"Journal #1",pages:['{"text":"I found him in the void.\\nAt first, I thought it was a statue - suspended in place, unmoving, almost lost to time. But the closer I got, the more certain I became: this wasn\'t a statue. It was a body locked in stasis, frozen between worlds...but still alive.\\n\\nSomehow..."}','{"text":"Not alive in the way most would recognize. I don\'t think he can speak. Maybe not even move. But I felt his presence. Like he was watching. Listening. Trapped just behind the veil of this world. There were journals near him, when I arrived. A few had already begun drifting into the void."}','{"text":"But some remained. Enough to piece together the truth.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n---->"}','{"text":"HE had broken the barrier.\\nYou probably know the one I mean. It wasn\'t a wall built by hands. IT was part of the dimension itself. Most never saw it. Fewer still understand what it was. And...\\n\\nAnyone who touches it unprepared would vanish in an instant."}','{"text":"That\'s what I believe happened to him. He didn\'t die, exactly.\\nBut his body, his soul... caught somewhere between \'here and not.\'"}'],resolved:1b,title:"Journal #1"}

{author:"GameTechBC",filtered_title:"Journal #3",pages:['{"text":"I call him...\\n\\nHe who gave up being, to keep a promise."}','{"text":"IF you\'re reading this, and you are that someone, look for a weird spike on a pedestal.\\nIt\'s not ordinary. If you\'re worthy enough, you can use that to save him from the stasis. But understand what that means."}','{"text":"You won\'t be waking him.\\n\\nYou\'ll be setting him free - by ending what remains of him here.\\n\\nWhatever left of his body can\'t hold on much longer.\\n\\nThat magic.. that stasis.. it\'s not life."}','{"text":"It\'s a prison made of everything he lost.\\n\\n\\nIt\'s not saving him  for us. Maybe it\'s just something we can do for him - so he can rest easier. Closer to the one he lost."}','{"text":"\\n\\n\\nWhatever you decide - do it for the right reasons. Not glory. Not power. But for the quiet, unseen stories that still deserve an ending..."}'],resolved:1b,title:"Journal #3"}

{author:"GameTechBC",filtered_title:"Journal #2",pages:['{"text":"The journals say he was looking for someone. Someone he lost. Someone who meant everything. And to find her, he walked a path no one else dared.\\n\\n\\"Breaking the barrier without hurting the creature in it\'s center wasn\'t so easy.\\""}','{"text":"That line stuck with me. He did it without violence. Without killing. That alone is something worth remembering.\\n\\nBut grief... Grief often blinds us."}','{"text":"There were things he didn\'t account for. Fundamental truths buried deep beneath the laws of this dimension. Things I won\'t write down here. If that knowledge ever ender up in the wrong hands, none of us would be safe.\\n\\n-- Definitely not because I\'m lazy."}','{"text":"I\'m not a mage. Not really. I just make some spells staying in the void here as my hobby. But I know enough to say this: what he did was near impossible.\\n\\nAnd he did it anyway. "}','{"text":"So, we built this place around him. A structure to keep his form safe. To wait - just in case someone more capable than me comes along. Someone who might be able to pull him back."}'],resolved:1b,title:"Journal #2"}

{filtered_title: "Reality", pages: ["{\"text\":\"The world was changing. Machines, steam, metal—people believed that was the future. They laughed at magic, called it a child's story. But I knew better. I swore I would prove them wrong.\"}"], title: "Reality", author: "Unknown Mage", resolved: 1}

{filtered_title: "Regret", pages: ["{\"text\":\"No one ever showed me her body. No one ever told me she was gone. I know she is out there, somewhere. And if I have to tear the End apart to find her, I will...\"}"], title: "Regret", author: "Unknown Mage", resolved: 1}
